concepts.title: Historian as Guardian of Sanity (MacCulloch)
concepts.excerpt: Imagine a country rector in mid-century England. Ridiculous huge house, can't afford to heat it, no money in the bank.

concepts.title: Historian as Non-Directive Counselor (MacCulloch)
concepts.excerpt: Perell asks MacCulloch what metaphors he uses for the historian's role.

concepts.title: Skeptical-Then-Sympathetic Historical Stance (MacCulloch)
concepts.excerpt: A young historian sits down across from you and asks: what are the core principles?

concepts.title: "Yes, But" Framework — Historical Balance (MacCulloch)
concepts.excerpt: You're reading Churchill on the Second World War. The prose is beautiful.

concepts.title: "May Have" Discipline & Degrees of Confidence (MacCulloch)
concepts.excerpt: A historian is writing about Thomas Cromwell, and the documentary record runs out at a moment where something clearly happened that the sources don't describe.

concepts.title: Declared Biases as Historian Ethic (MacCulloch)
concepts.excerpt: You pick up MacCulloch's book on the history of Christianity. The introduction starts with what looks like a strange detour: he tells you who he is.

concepts.title: Secondary Sources Before Primary — Cliche Mapping (MacCulloch)
concepts.excerpt: The standard advice from craft books and graduate seminars runs like this: go to the primary sources.

concepts.title: Sense of Place as Research Methodology (MacCulloch)
concepts.excerpt: MacCulloch is in Moscow. He is filming a BBC documentary about Ivan the Terrible.

concepts.title: Counterfactual History as Methodology
concepts.excerpt: Franz Ferdinand's driver took a wrong turn.

concepts.title: Cross-Discipline Nerving as Historiographic Engine (MacCulloch)
concepts.excerpt: If you read MacCulloch's interview attentively, the same structural move keeps appearing in different costumes.

concepts.title: Entertainment Without Fetish — Wolfson Criterion (MacCulloch)
concepts.excerpt: MacCulloch judges the Wolfson History Prize. Roughly 180 books a year cross his desk.

concepts.title: Defeat as Historian's Cognitive Equipment (Thucydides via MacCulloch)
concepts.excerpt: Thucydides — the man often called the first great historian — was, before he wrote, an Athenian general.

concepts.title: Lunacy as Historical Explanatory Variable (MacCulloch)
concepts.excerpt: Outside Edinburgh stands Rosslyn Chapel. Tourists go there now because of Dan Brown's novels and the mystical theories that have accreted around the place.

concepts.title: "Elizabeth Was a Carrot" — Pedagogy as Play (MacCulloch)
concepts.excerpt: A room full of sixth-formers. MacCulloch is at the front. He hands them a list of twenty statements about Elizabeth the First.

concepts.title: Lahiri's Historiographic Method for Ashoka
concepts.excerpt: Walk up to Ashoka with only his own edicts in hand and you get a man who appears, fully formed, at the moment of his Buddhist conversion.

concepts.title: Landscape Mediates the Edict Meaning
concepts.excerpt: A traveler in 260 BCE arrives at Maski in Karnataka and hears the king's first Minor Rock Edict read aloud on a rocky outcrop tucked inside the Durgada Gudda ridge, in a cavern visible only to those who come deliberately to the spot.

concepts.title: Ashoka's Deliberate Genealogical Silence
concepts.excerpt: Stand in front of any Ashokan rock — the one in the rice fields at Maski, the one on the steep hillside above Brahmagiri, the great panel at Girnar with all fourteen edicts cut in neat columns.

concepts.title: The Emperor's Afterlife — Buddhist vs Political Memory
concepts.excerpt: Ashoka died around 232 BCE. The Mauryan dynasty collapsed within roughly fifty years — by ~180 BCE, when the general Pushyamitra Shunga overthrew the last Mauryan king Brhidratha and founded the Shunga dynasty.
